questions.history: Pass the existing source as the third element. Inspect identity, hasValue("name") and getValue("name") on that element.
questions.prediction: The parent wraps it as a bean and fails to expose its named parameter. The merge should return the same source object with name present and equal to source.
questions.basis: The Javadoc promises use as-is. The supplied object independently defines its own values, and its JavaBean property names do not include name.
questions.refutation: The returned element is a wrapper, reports the name absent, or yields a different value.

questions.history: Submit just the map and the bean, exercising both collection and Object-varargs overloads on fresh tables.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should yield two parameters in input order, with names map and bean, then store (1,map) and (2,bean).
questions.basis: Map keys and bean getters independently supply distinct values for the same SQL parameters.
questions.refutation: An overload loses an element, reorders the names, or stores a different row.

questions.history: On the merge, keep the mixed array and change the original source’s name to revised after createBatch but before batchUpdate.
questions.prediction: A successful commit should leave exactly (1,map), (2,bean), (3,revised). The precise JDBC success counts may be driver-dependent.
questions.basis: Object identity means a subsequent mutation is visible. Independent row readback tests how the actual named-parameter binder consumes that object.
questions.refutation: Conversion passes its identity check but binding fails or readback shows source, a missing row, or a different id-to-name pairing.
